decisions.rationale: The original BHSA word.sp table explicitly defines art as article at line 17. OLiA Article at original XML line 1682 denotes the lexical article POS; this is a category-level exact alignment, not a claim about individual Hebrew token definiteness.

BHSA sp.md line 22 explicitly assigns prep to preposition; OLiA Preposition at line 525 denotes preposed adpositions. Hebrew prepositions may attach graphically to words, but this TF POS value maps the lexical class rather than token segmentation.

BHSA sp.md line 23 describes conj generically as conjunction; OLiA Conjunction at line 356 is the generic connective POS. Do not narrow to coordinating or subordinating conjunction without a source feature.

BHSA sp.md line 24 says personal pronoun, but OLiA PersonalPronoun at line 2189 explicitly narrows the class to irreflexive personal pronouns; the BHSA source alone does not verify this exclusion. Retain native-only pending lexical inspection.

BHSA sp.md line 25 explicitly defines prde as demonstrative pronoun; OLiA DemonstrativePronoun at line 1935 is the matching pronoun subclass. Do not conflate prde with a general determiner category or Syriac pron.

BHSA sp.md line 26 explicitly defines prin as interrogative pronoun, whereas inrg at line 29 is an interrogative particle. OLiA InterrogativePronoun at line 2135 denotes the corresponding pro-form subclass.

BHSA sp.md line 27 explicitly glosses intj as interjection, and OLiA Interjection at XML line 307 defines the same morphosyntactic category. This is not a generalized assertion about discourse speech acts.
BHSA sp.md line 28 explicitly defines nega as negative particle. OLiA NegativeParticle at XML line 3684 means a particle expressing negation, not abstract logical negation or morphological polarity.
BHSA sp.md line 29 explicitly defines inrg as interrogative particle, not interrogative pronoun prin. OLiA InterrogativeParticle at XML line 3812 defines a particle used to form a question.
Pinned ETCBC linksyr word_grammar line 86 explicitly glosses Syriac sp=conj as conjunction. OLiA Conjunction line 356 is the matching generic class; no narrower coordination subtype is assumed.

Pinned Syriac word_grammar line 87 glosses sp=inrg only as interrogative; it does not identify the expression as a particle versus an adverb or pronoun. No exact InterrogativeParticle target is asserted without more specific corpus evidence.
Pinned Syriac word_grammar line 88 explicitly glosses sp=intj as interjection. OLiA Interjection line 307 is the corresponding class and does not entail an extra pragmatic annotation.

Pinned Syriac word_grammar line 89 glosses sp=nega merely as negative; it does not establish that the class contains only particles rather than other polarity forms. No exact NegativeParticle class projection is justified by this source alone.
Pinned Syriac word_grammar line 90 explicitly calls sp=prep preposition; OLiA Preposition at original XML line 525 is a preposed adposition. No assumptions about bound morpheme boundaries are needed.

Pinned Syriac word_grammar line 91 describes sp=pron as general pronoun; OLiA Pronoun at XML line 1860 is the corresponding unspecialized category. It must not be mapped to any particular BHSA personal, demonstrative or interrogative pronoun subclass.
